title: One celebrity key puts a single database shard under all the load
summary: The database dashboard says there is plenty of headroom. One shard disagrees.

logs.text: shard 3 is handling {rand:68-72}% of writes for key user:9001
shards 0 to 2 idle at under 10% each, shard 3 queueing

deploys.text: posts table resharded by user id, 4 shards

lines: Averaged across shards the database reads {m:db-primary.saturation|pct}. The average hides the one shard that is on fire.

hint: Averages lie. Look at how the load is spread across shards, not how much there is.
rootCause: A single viral post made one key take about 70% of the traffic. The shard key sent all of it to one shard, so that shard was overloaded while the other three sat nearly idle and the database total looked fine.
concept: Sharding only helps if load spreads evenly. A hot key or a bad shard key concentrates traffic on one shard, and no amount of total capacity helps. Re-keying or splitting the hot key spreads it across shards again.

harmfulWhy.scale-service: More app pods opened more connections to a database that was already at its limit. The hot shard stayed hot and the database started refusing connections as well.
harmfulWhy.failover: The replica has the same shard layout, so the hot key followed it. Promotion also dropped capacity for a while, so the database got slower on top of an overloaded shard.

guideTitle: A short course on sharding a database
